info.title: HALo — Hardware Abstraction Layer and I/O
info.description:
Robot sensor API with UDP transport and HTTP documentation.

## Discovery

`GET /discover` lists all sensors with their endpoints and UDP ports.

## Per-Sensor Endpoints

Each sensor has its own routes:
- `GET /{sensor_id}/info` - schema, commands, UDP packet format
- `GET /{sensor_id}/data` - current data snapshot
- `POST /{sensor_id}/command` - send a command
- `POST /{sensor_id}/estop` - emergency stop (supported drivers only)

## UDP Protocol

Packets: `| version (1B) | msg_type (1B) | seq_num (2B LE) | JSON payload |`

### Data Subscription
Send **Subscribe (0x01)** to the sensor's data port. The robot pushes **Data (0x03)** packets to your address continuously. Send **Unsubscribe (0x02)** to stop.

### Commands
- **REST sensors**: Send **Command (0x10)**, get **CommandAck (0x11)**.
- **Stream sensors** (CAN watchdog): Send **Command (0x10)** continuously at the advertised interval; every packet is processed once and acknowledged with **CommandAck (0x11)**.

post.summary: Kinova Gen2 6DOF (sim) - Send Command
post.description:

get.summary: List available log files
get.description: Returns the directory tree under `LOG_DIR` as `{date → {hour → {sensors[], inputs}}}`. Use `GET /logs/file/{path}` with the relative path to download a specific CSV.

get.summary: Download a log file
get.description: Download a CSV file from the log tree. `path` is a forward-slash-separated path relative to `LOG_DIR`, e.g. `2026-05-02/14/kinova_arm.csv` or `2026-05-02/14/inputs.csv`. Path traversal (`..`) is rejected.

post.summary: Upload flat_endpoints.json
post.description:
Upload the ODrive `flat_endpoints.json` file to enable config read/write on all nodes.

**How to get the file** (on your dev machine where odrivetool is installed):
```
python3 -c "import odrive, os; print(os.path.dirname(odrive.__file__))"
```Then find `flat_endpoints.json` in that directory.

**Upload via curl:**
```
curl -X POST http://raspberrypi.local:8080/odrive/endpoints \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @flat_endpoints.json
```

Or paste the file contents directly in the request body below.

post.summary: Reload all sensors (process bounce)
post.description: Exits the API process so the systemd unit restarts it. Every driver re-runs its connect path, which is the reliable fix when one device (typically the Kinova arm) didn't answer on cold boot. The API is unavailable for ~3–5 s during the bounce, and active UDP subscriptions / streaming command sessions are dropped.

example.message: process is exiting; systemd will restart the service in ~2s

Read current data from **VectorNav VN-300 (sim)**.

This mirrors what you'd get via UDP subscription on port 25000.

get.summary: VectorNav VN-300 (sim) - Read Endpoint
get.description:
Read a single endpoint from **VectorNav VN-300 (sim)** by path. Returns `{path, value, type}`.

Paths come from `GET /vectornav_sim/endpoints`.

get.summary: VectorNav VN-300 (sim) - List Endpoints
get.description: List the readable endpoints exposed by **VectorNav VN-300 (sim)**. Drivers declare the available fields and paths. Use `GET /vectornav_sim/endpoint/{path}` to read a single value.

get.summary: VectorNav VN-300 (sim) - Info
get.description:
Full schema and UDP protocol details for **VectorNav VN-300 (sim)**.

Mode: REST (one-shot)
Data UDP port: 25000
Command UDP port: 25001

200.description: Sensor info with schemas and UDP protocol

oneOf.description: Request/response: client sends a single command, server replies once.

Streaming: client sends Command packets continuously at `interval_ms`.
Each packet is processed as it arrives — the server does not loop or
re-send anything. Typical use: CAN control loops sending ODrive setpoints.

interval_ms.description: Expected client send interval in milliseconds.

CommandMode.description: Whether commands are one-shot or arrive as a continuous stream.

DataDelivery.description: A driver declares its delivery model; the transport handles every subscriber.

FieldDescriptor.description: Describes one field in a data or command schema (for OpenAPI docs).

requires_ready.description:
Drivers declare command constraints; transport/UI code never infers them
from a hardware brand or a particular command name.
